brief: Goldman's positioning note: SPX/NDX trade within a weekly straddle of generational highs while gross exposure rises and net exposure stays contained, so risk is being added without added directional conviction. Panic pricing is absent (GS panic index sub 1) despite weak sentiment (GS sentiment -0.9, AAII bears ~50, 70% of SPX below the 50dma) and peak-percentile fear in bond vol (MOVE) and CDX, even as VIX sits in the low teens. Prime brokerage: hedge funds net sold equities this week (long sales in macro, short sales in single stocks); gross L/S exposure rose to the 71st percentile while net fell to the 7th. Asset managers also derisked, cutting equity futures length from 48% to 36% of open interest. Separately, CTAs are near-maximum short across the US Treasury curve (2y 81%, 5y 92%, 10y 99%, 30y 100% of max short, ~$390bn notional). The desk argues this backdrop could give way to a year-end position-squaring chase, triggered by midterms, tech earnings, or a Middle East detente, and separately likes shorting non-profitable tech (GSXUNPTC) given rising anxiety about a 10Y approach toward 6%.
